title: Coproducts of schemes: open coprojections with disjoint images covering
statement: Let $I$ be a set and $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ a family of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Then a coproduct $X=\coprod_{i\in I}X_i$ exists in the category of schemes: there are morphisms $\iota_i:X_i\to X$ such that for every scheme $Y$ and every family of morphisms $f_i:X_i\to Y$ there is a unique morphism $f:X\to Y$ with $f\circ\iota_i=f_i$ for all $i$. Moreover each $\iota_i$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], the images $\iota_i(X_i)$ are pairwise disjoint for $i\ne j$, and $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}\iota_i(X_i)$; consequently each $\iota_i(X_i)$ is open and closed in $X$ (its complement is the open set $\bigcup_{j\ne i}\iota_j(X_j)$).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 26.14.1 (Tag 01JB, label lemma-glue) and Lemma 26.14.2 (Tag 01JC, label lemma-glue-schemes), applied to the glueing data with $U_{ii}=X_i$ and $U_{ij}=\varnothing$ for $i\ne j$: the glued scheme with the open subspaces $U_i\cong X_i$, and the first mapping property $\Mor(X,Y)=\{(f_i)_{i\in I}\}$ (no compatibility condition since $U_{ij}=\varnothing$)
